A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, On the Power of Context-Enhanced Learning in LLMs. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison despite pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original Llama translation experiments, representation and parameter analyses, phrasebook-recovery measurements, and surrogate-model and constructed-transformer experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a controlled comparison of perturbing used versus unused phrasebook rules.

M1.justification: The context-enhanced learning algorithm, dropout curricula, CoT internalization, and optimization procedures are retained. New Definition G.8 is presented as an equivalent representation of the existing surrogate; it does not establish a changed training or inference method.

E1.justification: Both retain the same synthetic MLT coverage, including Llama experiments with d=5 and n=8/10 and surrogate experiments up to d=20. The new perturbation control refines an existing mechanistic experiment without extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains No Context, Fixed Dropout, Annealing Dropout, No Dropout, Wrong Context, and No ICL. Recovery experiments retain the same decoding and token-filtering strategies. The new perturbation control introduces no competing learning method.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 changes the main perturbation experiment from replacing an entire phrasebook to randomly replacing outputs of ten rules used by the input translation. V2 also tests unused-rule perturbations. The earlier whole-phrasebook experiment remains in Appendix C.2.

E4.justification: New Figure 8 compares perturbations of used and unused rules to test whether representation changes reflect semantic relevance or merely context position. This strengthens one existing mechanistic analysis; the other ablations and supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 retains averaging over 20 permutations of phrasebook text. Neither version adds or changes training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: Figure 3 contains updated heatmaps under the revised perturbation protocol, and new Figure 8 reports negligible representation changes from unused-rule perturbations. The earlier whole-phrasebook findings survive in v2 Figure 9. Figure 2 and recovery Tables 2, 4, and 5 retain their results.

T1.justification: Definition G.8 and Equation (20) add an explicit block-matrix derivation claiming equivalence when context matrices are concatenated with the input. The printed recurrence omits the HardMax operation required by Definition G.7. Existing sample-complexity theorems and proofs otherwise remain unchanged apart from renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction overview, and conclusion retain the same central claims about sample efficiency, required ICL capability, improved gradient information, and difficulty recovering contextual training material. The new control supports an existing claim.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly argues that the unused-rule control rules out a purely positional explanation of layerwise representation changes. Existing qualifications about synthetic tasks, surrogate-based theory, and limited recovery attacks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 specifies how to implement the revised intervention: sample ten used rules and replace their outputs with randomly chosen tuples. Training hyperparameters, optimization details, training-text formats, and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Choi et al. (2025) on contextual fine-tuning and Pfau et al. (2024) on hidden computation. The masked-language-modeling and infilling discussion moves from Section 6 to Appendix D without substantive revision.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the perturbation description, expands explanations, relocates one related-work paragraph, removes the appendix table of contents, and updates publication information. Most prose is retained. Section 3.1 also introduces an apparent missing negation, calling the unprepared base model ICL-capable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is revised and Figure 8 adds a two-row used/unused-rule comparison. Existing whole-phrasebook plots are retained as Figure 9. Caption expansions, display relocation, and appendix reflow change presentation without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The used-versus-unused-rule control provides better evidence for semantic, sequential processing while preserving the original results. This is a limited empirical improvement. It is tempered by the contradictory wording in Section 3.1 and the missing HardMax in new Equation (20), although the retained learning procedures and sample-complexity proofs are unchanged.
